Questions.content: What is the number of weeks in a month that will be used for the conversion? This assumption can affect the accuracy of the monthly usage calculation.
What is the standard number of weeks in a month being assumed for this calculation, and how will variations in the actual number of weeks per month affect the monthly usage?

Answers.content: For the conversion from weekly usage to monthly usage, a common approximation is to assume there are 4 weeks in a month. This assumption simplifies the calculation and provides a reasonable estimate for most practical purposes. However, it's important to note that this is an approximation, as the actual number of days in a month can vary (some months have 30 days, others have 31, and February has 28 or 29).

The standard number of weeks in a month is typically assumed to be 4 for most calculations. However, since a month can have either 4 or approximately 4.35 weeks (considering an average month as 1/12 of a year and a non-leap year having 365 days), this assumption can lead to slight variations in the calculated monthly usage.

If we assume there are exactly 4 weeks in a month, then:
- Miguel uses 2 pads per week.
- Each pad contains 30 sheets.
- Therefore, he uses \(2 \text{ pads/week} \times 30 \text{ sheets/pad} = 60 \text{ sheets/week}\).
- Assuming 4 weeks in a month, the monthly usage would be \(60 \text{ sheets/week} \times 4 \text{ weeks/month} = 240 \text{ sheets/month}\).

However, if we consider an average month to have approximately 4.35 weeks:
- The weekly usage remains 60 sheets.
- Thus, the monthly usage would be \(60 \text{ sheets/week} \times 4.35 \text{ weeks/month} \approx 261 \text{ sheets/month}\).

This difference is due to the varying lengths of months and can affect the accuracy of the calculation depending on whether a more precise value (like 4.35) or a simpler assumption (like 4) is used.
